title: ICSE Class 10 History, Chapter 7: Quit India Movement, Step by Step
subtitle: For students who find history hard. The war and the resignation of the Congress ministries, the Pakistan demand, the August Offer, the Cripps Mission and why it failed, the Japanese threat, the Quit India Resolution, the movement, the repression and its significance, held together by one idea (cash now, not a post-dated cheque), in small steps with model answers, quick checks, an exam toolkit and a last-minute revision sheet. Follows the ICSE Class 10 syllabus, Chapter 7 (Quit India Movement), in the order of Total History & Civics.

**One idea runs through this whole chapter: cash now, not a post-dated cheque.** In the war, Britain only offered **promises for later** (the **August Offer** and **Cripps**). With **Japan at the door**, Gandhi said the British must **quit India now**: **Do or Die** (8 August 1942).

children.label: About this roadmap
children.desc:
**What it is.** A step-by-step path through Chapter 7, *Quit India Movement*, of the History part of the ICSE Class 10 History and Civics syllabus. It follows the order of *Total History & Civics* for Class 10.

**Who it is for.** Class 10 students who find history hard, and want to understand this chapter and score decent marks in it. It also works for revision, and for the teachers and parents helping them: the last milestone is written for adults.

**The one idea.** Cash now, not a post-dated cheque. In the Second World War, Britain only offered promises for later (the August Offer and the Cripps Mission). With Japan at India's door, Gandhi said the British must quit India now: Do or Die.

**How it is different from the textbook.** The textbook moves quickly through the war years. Here one picture, **cash now, not a post-dated cheque**, links the resignations, the August Offer, Cripps and Quit India, so the causes make sense. Every answer is a **point plus one fact**, with fresh model answers.

**What is inside.**
- 10 milestones and 37 small steps. The 29 solid steps are the core path. The dashed ones are optional.
- 36 practice questions with hidden answers.
- 25 click-to-check questions that say right or wrong, and why: a quick check after each of the 5 main milestones, and a 10-question self-test.
- A **last-minute revision sheet**: every date, key term, name and trap on one page.
- *Start here* fixes the basic skills the chapter needs, and *Check yourself* shows which ones to work on.
- Optional: picture study and two structured challenge questions, and a section for teachers and parents with a 5-period lesson plan, the mistakes to watch for and a 5-minute exit ticket.

**Can you trust it?** Dates, names and places follow the textbook, and the few slips found in it are pointed out gently. A computer program checks that every date sits in the right order and every click-to-check answer is marked right. All the model answers are written fresh, so students still get fresh practice from their textbook. If you spot a mistake, use **Report a problem** at the top of the page.

**Not official.** This is a free, independent resource. It follows the ICSE syllabus but is not made or endorsed by CISCE or by any publisher. It is shared under the **CC BY-SA 4.0** licence: you may copy, adapt and share it, as long as you credit it and share your version the same way.

children.label: Check yourself (2 minutes)
children.desc: Four quick questions. Write your answers first, then open each box. If you get one wrong, do the step named in the answer.

faq.q: 1. Who declared India at war in 1939?
faq.a: **Lord Linlithgow.** Wrong? Do *Who's who in this chapter*.

faq.q: 2. What is a post-dated cheque?
faq.a: A cheque you can only cash **later**. Wrong? Do *Cash now, not a post-dated cheque*.

faq.q: 3. What was Gandhi's call in 1942?
faq.a: **Do or Die.** Wrong? Do *Cash now, not a post-dated cheque*.

faq.q: 4. How many points for a 2-mark answer?
faq.a: **Two**, each with **one fact**. Wrong? Do *How ICSE asks, and the answer shape*.

children.label: Who's who in this chapter
children.desc:
- **Lord Linlithgow:** Viceroy who took India into the war.
- **Winston Churchill:** British Prime Minister from 1940.
- **Sir Stafford Cripps:** British minister who came with an offer in 1942.
- **M.A. Jinnah:** leader of the **Muslim League**.
- **Gandhi** and the Congress; underground heroes **Jayaprakash Narayan, Ram Manohar Lohia, Aruna Asaf Ali**.

faq.q: Your turn: which Viceroy declared India at war in 1939?
faq.a: **Lord Linlithgow.**

children.label: Cash now, not a post-dated cheque
children.desc:
This chapter has **one idea**. A **post-dated cheque** is a cheque you can only cash **later**.

- In the Second World War, Britain needed India's help.
- It kept offering **promises for later**: the **August Offer** (1940) and the **Cripps Mission** (1942).
- Gandhi called Cripps's offer **'a post-dated cheque on a failing bank'**.
- With **Japan at India's door**, India wanted **freedom now**.
- So on **8 August 1942** the Congress told the British: **Quit India**. Gandhi's call: **Do or Die**.

faq.q: Your turn: why did Gandhi call Cripps's offer a 'post-dated cheque'?
faq.a: It promised **dominion status** only **after the war**, not freedom **now**.

children.label: How ICSE asks, and the answer shape
children.desc:
ICSE asks history in three ways.

- **Multiple choice:** 1 mark. Pick one option.
- **Short answer:** usually 2 marks. Write **two points**.
- **Structured question:** parts (a), (b), (c), worth 3 or 4 marks each. Write **one point per mark**.

Each point has **one fact**: a name, a date or a place. A point without a fact looks vague and loses marks.

**Model answer.** *State two causes of the Quit India Movement.*

- The **failure of the Cripps Mission** (March 1942): it offered only **dominion status after the war**.
- The **Japanese threat**: Japan had taken **Burma** and was nearing **Assam**; Gandhi said British presence invited an invasion.

faq.q: Your turn: what is wrong with this answer? 'The British did not listen to Indians.'
faq.a: It has **no fact**. Add one: for example, *'The Cripps Mission offered only dominion status after the war.'*

topics.label: The war and the deadlock, 1939 to 1940
topics.desc:
**Goal:** explain why the Congress ministries resigned, the League's new demand, and why the August Offer failed.

Practice: in the chapter exercises in *Total History & Civics*, Exercise I (short answers) on the Congress's condition, the resignations and the August Offer.

children.label: War without asking
children.desc:
- Since **1937** the Congress ran governments in **most provinces**.
- In **September 1939** the Second World War began. **Lord Linlithgow** declared India **at war** without asking Indian leaders.
- The Congress asked: how can an **enslaved** nation fight for others' freedom? India must be **declared free**, or given **real power** now.
- Linlithgow offered only **dominion status** someday.
- So the Congress ministries **resigned** (October and November 1939).

The **Muslim League** was delighted. It celebrated a **'Day of Deliverance'** and offered friendship to the British.

faq.q: Your turn: why did the Congress ministries resign in 1939?
faq.a: The Viceroy **declared India at war** without consulting Indians, and would not promise **freedom**.

children.label: The League asks for Pakistan
children.desc:
- After the 1937 elections, Jinnah said Muslims could not expect **justice** from the Congress.
- In **1940**, at Lahore, the League demanded a **separate state** for Muslims: **Pakistan**.
- Jinnah said India should be divided into **two** states.

faq.q: Your turn: what did the League demand in 1940?
faq.a: A **separate state** for Muslims, **Pakistan**, by dividing India into **two** states.

children.label: The August Offer, 1940

faq.q: Your turn: why did the Congress and the League both reject the August Offer?
faq.a: The Congress wanted **independence**, not dominion status later; the League wanted a clear promise of **Pakistan**.

topics.label: The Cripps Mission, 1942
topics.desc:
**Goal:** explain why Cripps came, what he offered, and why all sides said no.

Practice: in the chapter exercises in *Total History & Civics*, Exercise I on the Cripps proposals, and Exercise II (structured) question 1.

children.label: Why Cripps came
children.desc:
Early in 1942, **Japan** won victory after victory in Asia. It took **Burma** and came close to India.

Britain urgently needed India's **support**. So in **March 1942**, Prime Minister **Churchill** sent **Sir Stafford Cripps** to talk to all parties.

faq.q: Your turn: why was the Cripps Mission sent to India?
faq.a: Japan was **advancing** towards India, and Britain needed Indian **support** in the war.

children.label: What Cripps offered
children.desc:
- **Dominion status** for India **after** the war.
- A **constituent assembly** to write a constitution: members elected by the provincial legislatures, plus **princes' nominees**.
- Any province could **stay out** of the Indian Union and make its own constitution.
- Protection for **minorities**.
- During the war, **defence** stayed with the **British**.

faq.q: Your turn: how was the constitution-making body to be formed under Cripps?
faq.a: Members **elected** by the provincial legislatures, and **nominees** of the princely rulers.

children.label: Why everyone said no
children.desc:
- **Congress:** no **independence now**; **defence** stayed British; provinces could **break away**, which meant **partition**. Gandhi: ***'a post-dated cheque on a failing bank'***.
- **Muslim League:** Pakistan was **not** clearly promised.
- **Hindu Mahasabha:** it feared **partition**.
- **Sikhs, Christians, Anglo-Indians, labour:** too few **safeguards**.
- **People of the princely states:** their members would be chosen by **rulers**, not by them.

**Model answer.** *Give two reasons why the Congress rejected the Cripps proposals.*

- They offered only **dominion status after the war**, not **independence now**.
- Provinces could **stay out** of the Union, which could lead to the **partition** of India.

faq.q: Your turn: why did the people of the princely states object to Cripps?
faq.a: Their members would be **nominated by the rulers**, not elected by the **people**.

children.label: Quick check: the Cripps Mission
children.desc:
Three questions on this milestone. Click an answer to check it.

Wrong? Read the reason, then look back at the step it names.

quiz.q: Why was the Cripps Mission sent?
options: The Congress had asked for it
Japan was advancing and Britain needed Indian support

quiz.q: What did Cripps offer?
options: Dominion status after the war, and a constituent assembly

quiz.q: Gandhi called the Cripps proposals:
options: a post-dated cheque on a failing bank
quiz.why: Payable **later**, by a bank that might **fail**. See *Why everyone said no*.

topics.label: The Quit India Resolution, 1942
topics.desc:
**Goal:** explain the Japanese threat and the Quit India Resolution.

Practice: in the chapter exercises in *Total History & Civics*, Exercise I on the Japanese threat and the meaning of Quit India, and Exercise II question 2.

children.label: The Japanese at the door
children.desc:
- In **1942**, Japan attacked **Burma** and marched towards **Assam**.
- Gandhi argued: Japan wants to fight **Britain**, not India. **British presence** is what invites Japan.
- He said: *their withdrawal removes the **bait***.
- Leaders felt that only a **free** India could defend itself.

faq.q: Your turn: how did the Japanese threat lead to Quit India?
faq.a: Gandhi felt the **British presence** invited a Japanese **invasion**; if the British left, the reason for the attack would go.

children.label: The Quit India Resolution
children.desc:
- **July 1942:** the Congress Working Committee at **Wardha** passed the **Quit India Resolution**: British rule in India **must end immediately**.
- **8 August 1942:** the **All-India Congress Committee** confirmed it at **Bombay**.
- If the British did not leave, a **non-violent mass struggle** would begin under Gandhi.

faq.q: Your turn: where and when was the Quit India Resolution passed?
faq.a: First at **Wardha** (July 1942), then confirmed at **Bombay** on **8 August 1942**.

children.label: Do or Die
children.desc:
In his Bombay speech, Gandhi called on every Indian: ***'Do or Die'***.

- **Do:** act as a **free** person from now on.
- **Die:** be ready to give everything for freedom.

It was the **boldest** call of the whole struggle: no more waiting.

faq.q: Your turn: what did 'Do or Die' mean?
faq.a: Either **win freedom** now, or **die** trying: Indians should act as **free** people and accept any sacrifice.

children.label: Quick check: the Quit India Resolution
children.desc:
Three questions on this milestone. Click an answer to check it.

Wrong? Read the reason, then look back at the step it names.

quiz.q: Where was the Quit India Resolution first adopted?
quiz.why: The Working Committee at **Wardha**; the AICC **confirmed** it at **Bombay**. See *The Quit India Resolution*.

quiz.q: What was Gandhi's call to the people?
Why did Gandhi say the British should leave at once?
options: Their presence invited a Japanese invasion
quiz.why: 'Their withdrawal removes the **bait**.' See *The Japanese at the door*.

topics.label: The movement and the repression
topics.desc:
**Goal:** describe how the people rose, the underground and parallel governments, and how the British crushed them.

Practice: in the chapter exercises in *Total History & Civics*, Exercise I on the leaders and activities of the movement.

children.label: Leaders arrested, people rise
children.desc:
- Early on **9 August 1942**, before anything could start, **Gandhi** and all top leaders were **arrested**. The Congress was **banned**.
- Gandhi was held at the **Aga Khan Palace**, Pune; others at **Ahmednagar Fort**.
- Without leaders, people acted **on their own**: strikes, marches, and attacks on **symbols of British rule**: police stations, post offices, railway stations, telegraph lines.
- British rule **vanished** for a time in parts of UP, Bihar, Bengal, Odisha, Maharashtra and the south.

faq.q: Your turn: give two activities people undertook during Quit India.
faq.a: They held **strikes and demonstrations**, and attacked **symbols** of British rule like **police stations and railway stations**.

children.label: Parallel governments and the underground

faq.q: Your turn: name two places where parallel governments were set up.
faq.a: **Ballia** (eastern Uttar Pradesh) and **Satara** (Maharashtra).

children.label: Repression
children.desc:
The British struck with **great force**.

- The **press** was gagged.
- Crowds were **machine-gunned**, and some were **bombed from the air**.
- Villages paid huge **fines**; there were mass **floggings**.
- By the end of 1942, about **10,000** were killed and **60,000** arrested (your textbook's figures).

India had not seen such repression since **1857**. The movement was **crushed** by 1944.

faq.q: Your turn: give two repressive measures used against Quit India.
faq.a: The **press** was gagged, and crowds were **fired on**, even **bombed** from the air.

children.desc:

options: Gandhi and the top leaders were arrested
quiz.why: Before the movement could even begin. See *Leaders arrested, people rise*.

quiz.q: Where were parallel governments set up?
Which leader worked underground during Quit India?
quiz.why: With **JP** and **Lohia**. See *Parallel governments and the underground*.

topics.label: The significance of Quit India
topics.desc:
**Goal:** explain the significance of the Quit India Movement.

Practice: in the chapter exercises in *Total History & Civics*, Exercise I on how Quit India showed the depth of national feeling, and Exercise II question 2.

children.label: Why Quit India mattered
children.desc:
The movement was **crushed**, but it changed everything:

- It showed how **deep** national feeling had become, and how much people would **sacrifice**.
- It made clear that Britain could **no longer rule India against the people's will**.
- **All** sections took part: students, workers, peasants, women, people of the **princely states**.
- **Independence** became the **only** agenda. The question now was **when and how** power would be handed over.
- New leaders rose; the **Congress Socialist Party** (Jayaprakash Narayan) grew strong.

**Model answer.** *State two points of significance of the Quit India Movement.*

- It showed the **depth** of national feeling and people's capacity for **sacrifice**.
- It made it clear that Britain could **not rule India against the people's will**; **independence** became the only agenda.

faq.q: Your turn: the movement was crushed. Was it a failure?
faq.a: **No.** It showed Britain could not rule India **against the people's will**, and made **independence** the only question left.

children.label: Quick check: why it mattered
children.desc:

topics.label: Exam toolkit: words and reasons
topics.desc: **Goal:** collect the easy marks: key terms, answers in the right shape, 'why' questions and dates.

children.label: Key terms to learn word for word
children.desc:
- **August Offer (1940):** Lord Linlithgow's offer of dominion status as the goal and a constitution-making body after the war.
- **Cripps Mission (1942):** Sir Stafford Cripps's offer of dominion status after the war, a constituent assembly, and the right of provinces to stay out.
- **Quit India Resolution (1942):** the Congress resolution that British rule in India must end immediately.
- **Do or Die:** Gandhi's call in 1942: win freedom or die trying.
- **Parallel government:** a people's government set up in place of British rule, as at Ballia, Tamluk and Satara.

faq.q: Your turn: cover the list. What did the Quit India Resolution demand?
faq.a: That **British rule in India must end immediately**.

children.label: Answers in the right shape
children.desc:
**Short answer (2 marks):** two points, each with **one fact**.

**Structured part (3 or 4 marks):** one point per mark. Start each point on a **new line**. Keep each to **one or two sentences**.

**Model answer.** *Mention three proposals of the Cripps Mission. (3 marks)*

- **Dominion status** for India **after** the war.
- A **constituent assembly** to frame a new constitution.
- Any province could **stay out** of the Indian Union.

**Three things that lose marks:** mixing up the **August Offer** (1940) and **Cripps** (1942); saying the resolution was passed only at **Bombay**; giving numbers or places with **no year**.

faq.q: Your turn: write a 2-mark answer. 'Why did the Muslim League reject the Cripps proposals?'
faq.a: They did **not clearly promise Pakistan**, and they planned a **single Indian Union**.

children.label: 'Why' questions: model answers
children.desc: Try each one in your notebook before you open it.

faq.q: Why did the Congress refuse to support the war at first?
faq.a: An **enslaved** India could not fight for others' **freedom**; it wanted to be **declared free** first.

faq.q: Why did the League celebrate a Day of Deliverance?
faq.a: It welcomed the **end** of Congress rule in the provinces.

faq.q: Why were the Cripps proposals called a post-dated cheque?
faq.a: They promised freedom (dominion status) only **after the war**.

faq.q: Why did the movement turn violent in places?
faq.a: The leaders were **arrested** at once, so people acted **without guidance**.

faq.q: Why is Quit India important though it was crushed?
faq.a: It proved British rule could **not continue** against the people's **will**.

children.label: Dates to learn
children.desc:
Read it top to bottom. Say each line aloud once.

- **September 1939:** Second World War; India declared at war.
- **October and November 1939:** Congress ministries resign.
- **1940:** Muslim League demands Pakistan.
- **8 August 1940:** August Offer.
- **March 1942:** Cripps Mission.
- **July 1942:** Quit India Resolution, Wardha.
- **8 August 1942:** AICC confirms it at Bombay; 'Do or Die'.
- **9 August 1942:** Gandhi and leaders arrested; the people rise.
- **1945:** War ends.

faq.q: Your turn: which came first, the August Offer or the Cripps Mission?
faq.a: The **August Offer** (1940); Cripps came in **1942**.

children.label: Picture study: who is this?
children.desc:
The exam may show a **picture** and ask who it is. Then it asks two or three facts. For each person, learn **who** and **two facts**.

- **Sir Stafford Cripps with Gandhi:** Cripps Mission, March 1942; 'post-dated cheque'.
- **Gandhi and Nehru in 1942:** Quit India Resolution; **Do or Die**.
- **Aruna Asaf Ali:** hoisted the flag at Bombay; led the **underground**.
- **Jayaprakash Narayan:** **underground** hero; Congress Socialist Party.
- **Ram Manohar Lohia:** underground leader; secret radio.
- **Jinnah:** **Pakistan** demand, 1940; rejected Cripps.

faq.q: Your turn: a picture of Cripps with Gandhi. What did Gandhi call Cripps's proposals?
faq.a: **'A post-dated cheque on a failing bank.'**

topics.label: Wrap up: last-minute revision and self-test
topics.desc: **Goal:** see the whole chapter on one page, then test yourself. Read the sheet the night before the exam and again on the morning.

children.label: Last-minute revision sheet
children.desc:
**The one idea:** **cash now, not a post-dated cheque.** In the war, Britain only offered **promises for later** (August Offer, Cripps). With **Japan at the door**, Gandhi said the British must **quit India now**: **Do or Die** (8 August 1942).

**Dates to know**
- **1937** Congress ministries in the provinces. **September 1939** Second World War; India declared at war.
- **October and November 1939** Congress ministries resign. **1940** League's Pakistan resolution. **8 August 1940** August Offer.
- **March 1942** Cripps Mission. **July 1942** Quit India Resolution at **Wardha**. **8 August 1942** confirmed at **Bombay**. **9 August 1942** leaders arrested.

**Key terms**
- **August Offer:** Linlithgow's promise of **dominion status** as the goal, a constitution-making body **after the war**, and **no constitution without the minorities' consent**.
- **Cripps Mission:** Sir Stafford Cripps's offer of **dominion status after the war**, a **constituent assembly**, and the right of provinces to **stay out**.
- **Quit India Resolution:** British rule in India **must end immediately**.
- **Parallel government:** a people's government set up in place of British rule.

**Key points**
- **Deadlock:** India dragged into the war **without consent**; ministries resign; League's **'Day of Deliverance'**; **Pakistan** demand (1940).
- **August Offer rejected:** Congress (no freedom, minority veto); League (no Pakistan).
- **Cripps rejected:** no **independence** now; provinces could **opt out** (partition); princes, not people, chose states' members; **defence** stayed British. Gandhi: **'a post-dated cheque on a failing bank'**.
- **Japanese threat:** Japan in **Burma**, heading for **Assam**; British presence was **bait**.
- **Movement:** leaders jailed (Gandhi at the **Aga Khan Palace**, Pune; others at **Ahmednagar Fort**); attacks on police stations, post offices, railways; parallel governments at **Ballia, Tamluk, Satara**; underground: **Jayaprakash Narayan, Ram Manohar Lohia, Aruna Asaf Ali**.
- **Repression:** press gagged; firing, even **bombing** from the air; about **10,000** killed and **60,000** arrested by the end of 1942.
- **Significance:** showed the **depth** of national feeling; Britain could **not rule against the people's will**; all sections took part; **independence** the only agenda; new leaders.

**Traps:** **Wardha** (July, Working Committee) first, then **Bombay** (8 August, AICC). The August Offer was **1940**, Cripps **1942**. 'Do or Die' is **Quit India**; 'Swaraj is my birthright' is **Tilak**.

topics.label: When you're ready: challenge questions
topics.desc: **For later.** These are like the harder questions at the end of the chapter. It is completely fine to skip this milestone the first time through.

children.label: Structured question: the Cripps Mission
children.desc:
A structured question in three parts. Write your answer first, then open the box.

- (a) Why was the mission sent? (3 marks)
- (b) Three proposals. (3 marks)
- (c) Why did the Congress and the League reject them? (4 marks)

faq.q: Model answer
faq.a:
(a) **Japan** was advancing towards India, and Britain needed India's **support** in the war.

(b) **Dominion status** after the war; a **constituent assembly**; provinces free to **stay out**.

(c) **Congress:** no freedom **now**; defence stayed British; provinces could break away. **League:** **Pakistan** was not promised.

children.label: Structured question: Quit India
children.desc:
A structured question in three parts. Write your answer first, then open the box.

- (a) Why was the resolution passed? (3 marks)
- (b) How did the government react? (3 marks)
- (c) Give its significance. (4 marks)

faq.q: Model answer
faq.a:
(a) The **failure of Cripps**; the **Japanese threat**; British presence seen as **bait** for Japan.

(b) Leaders **arrested** on 9 August 1942; Congress **banned**; firing and **bombing**; mass **arrests**.

(c) It showed the **depth** of national feeling; Britain could **not rule against the people's will**; **independence** became the only agenda.

topics.label: For teachers and parents
topics.desc:
**For the adults helping.** Students can skip this milestone.

The syllabus asks for the causes (failure of Cripps, Japanese threat), the Quit India Resolution and the significance of the movement. The resignations of 1939 and the August Offer set the scene.

children.label: How to help a student who is struggling
children.desc:
- Use the **post-dated cheque** picture: show a cheque dated years ahead and ask, 'Would you accept this?'
- Draw a timeline from **1939 to 1942** with only four stops: resignations, August Offer, Cripps, Quit India.
- Separate **Wardha** (July) and **Bombay** (8 August) clearly.
- Keep the repression facts short and calm.
- Ask: 'The movement was crushed. Did it fail?' Let students argue it.
- Insist on **one fact per point**.

children.label: A 5-period plan, with activities
children.desc:
- **Period 1:** Cash now; the war and the resignations; the Pakistan demand.
- **Period 2:** August Offer; Cripps Mission and why it failed. Exercise II question 1.
- **Period 3:** Japanese threat; the resolution; Do or Die.
- **Period 4:** The movement, the underground, the repression; significance. Exercise II question 2.
- **Period 5:** Revision sheet, self-test, exit ticket; Exercise I.

children.label: Mistakes to watch for
children.desc:
- Mixing up the **August Offer** and **Cripps**.
- Saying the resolution was first passed at **Bombay** (it was **Wardha**).
- Giving 'Swaraj is my birthright' for Quit India (that is **Tilak**).
- Saying the movement **won** independence in 1942.
- Forgetting **why** the Japanese threat mattered.
- Answers with **no dates**.

children.label: Exit ticket (5 minutes)
children.desc: Five short questions covering the main ideas. The answers are below.

faq.q: 1. Why did the Congress ministries resign?
faq.a: India was declared **at war without consent**.

faq.q: 2. What did Cripps offer?
faq.a: **Dominion status after the war** and a **constituent assembly**.

faq.q: 3. What did Gandhi call it?
faq.a: **A post-dated cheque on a failing bank.**

faq.q: 4. When was Quit India passed at Bombay?
5. Give one significance.
faq.a: Britain could **not rule against the people's will**.
